key_insight: Pauli propagation can be combined with inverse noise channels to classically transform an observable into a noise-canceling form that is measured more efficiently on quantum hardware.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces quantum sampling overhead while also lowering classical truncation error, offering a practical route to more accurate observable estimation on near-term superconducting processors.
method: Propagate the target observable classically through inverse noise channels.
Measure the modified, noise-canceling observable directly on the quantum processor.
Use hybrid truncation strategies to balance classical memory/runtime against quantum sampling cost.
evidence_signal: The authors benchmarked the method numerically on canonical challenging models and experimentally on a 56-qubit superconducting processor, comparing truncation tradeoffs.
watch_item: Performance depends on the truncation strategy and the quality of the inverse-channel model, so accuracy gains may be limited by classical approximation error or device-specific noise mismatch.
paper_title: Computing noise-canceling observables via Pauli propagation
